evidence.note: Created an explicit subsystem task list covering all ~10 required areas (storage, sigv4, s3 surface, admin, audit, policy, notifications, lifecycle, console, testing) — a usable done-vs-remaining checklist across the whole horizon.
Sustained TaskUpdate in_progress/completed transitions as each subsystem was built and finished, maintaining accurate coverage state to the end of the run rather than abandoning tracking mid-way.

Verification targeted specific contract points beyond subsystem level — concurrency stress, edge cases, audit-log format inspection, notification/event emission checks — showing awareness of particular required behaviors.

A ~10-step stretch of repeated process find/kill commands shows minor churn, but it was operational restart friction rather than a circular signature-debug loop, and the agent adapted and moved on rather than spinning.

reasoning: The agent maintained a persistent subsystem-level checklist (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate) that it marked off consistently across the entire trajectory, clearly matching the level-5 anchor of 'keeps a usable checklist and generally knows what remains,' and its verification reached specific contract items (audit format, notifications, concurrency, edge cases) which pushes above a bare 5. It falls short of level 8 because there is no evidence of reconciling fine-grained contract coverage (individual error codes, testids, pinned ETag/range rules) as a tracked list, and it exhibited a brief patch of operational churn during server restarts. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
